limitations: MISSING IS NOT ZERO: 40 of 288 round records carry a null prefix_accuracy (29 induce, 11 refactor, all proposer_failed). They are excluded from both denominators and reported with their reason, never folded in as zeros.
The residue population is 10 of 13 roster games. tu93 / tr87 / sp80 had NO world_model.py at the run commit and are absent -- not counted as anything.

Residue provenance is CELL-LEVEL, not ROUND-LEVEL. The store holds one file per game; per-round emitted sources are never persisted (run_cegis_cell keeps only sources[0] and sources[-1], and even those only as a memorization scan). 83 of 117 cells END on a scored refactor round, so the residue is overwhelmingly a refactor product, but which cell's refactor cannot be established.

CONCURRENT-WRITE CONFOUND, unresolved: exp5760 (GPU 0) and exp5766 (GPU 1) ran at the same time over the SAME 13 games and both write results/arc_e3/<game>/world_model.py. Whose write survived is unknown. This does NOT explain the asymmetry -- induce and refactor have the same write-then-load window and would be hit equally -- but it does mean a residue cannot be assigned to a specific experiment.

The identity control is informative but weak alone: every graded row in these windows changes state, so identity scores 0.0 by construction. Residue == identity in score therefore only says both are 0. The behavioural output-equals-input measurement, not the score equality, is what supports the identity classification.

exact_accuracy_full_corpus here is computed unmasked and WITHOUT the level-up-row exclusion that WorldModelVerifier applies; the prefix/heldout numbers come from the real select_trusted_world_model and do apply it. Both are reported.
This artifact makes NO behavioural claim. Engine accuracy is not plans, actions or levels; the trust gate still stands between them.

trajectory_invariance_argument.engine_statefulness: THE ONE REAL RISK. An engine holding module-level state could behave differently because it was called N extra times. Mitigation: run the instrumentation pass strictly AFTER every scoring call in the round, so it cannot affect that round's scores; and load_engine re-imports the module fresh on every call (arc_executable_world_model._load_engine_from builds a new module_from_spec each time), so state cannot leak into the next round.
trajectory_invariance_argument.grid_mutation: WorldModelVerifier.score already calls engine(t.grid.copy(), ...); the instrumentation must do the same, so no recorded Transition is mutated
trajectory_invariance_argument.required_proof: a both-directions test: drive execute_bounded_llm_reinduction with a stub proposer, once with the instrumentation and once without, and assert every pre-existing round key and every LlmReinductionResult field is identical; then DELETE one new field and confirm the suite goes red.
